text.p: Photran Corp said Friday it received a new $1.4 million order for ITO-coated glass from Wintek Corp, its largest customer, at a 17 percent unit price increase over previous orders.
Photran expects to begin shipping at the new price July 1, 1997.
The company also received a $500,000 order from a new Taiwanese customer.
Photran manufactures high performance optical and electrically conductive thin film coated products using proprietary process technologies.
The company also entered an agreement with Wintek to retain ownership of a new production line.
Photran had previously said that Wintek, which accounted for 87 percent of its 1996 sales, would purchase an ITO coating line and pay Photran to operate it.

"Our agreement with Wintek enables us to retain the production capacity we need to boost revenues, expand our customer base and produce not only TN grade ITO-coated glass, but also higher margin, specialty products," Paul Fink, chief financial officer, said in a statement.
Under the agreement, Photran will repay the $500,000 down payment to Wintek over the next five months.
Photran said its second production line will boost its capacity by almost 200 percent, to 6.8 million units annually.
Photran has begun aggressively seeking customers to take advantage of its enhanced capacity.

The company also said it reopened negotiations with its former Chinese joint venture partner, the Shenzen WABO Group Co Ltd, which disclosed plans for a joint venture. In April, it began arbitration proceedings seeking $4.4 million in reimbursement and damages from Photran.
